newsitem.title: THAILAND: Poor Thai villagers set to end marathon protest.
newsitem.headline: Poor Thai villagers set to end marathon protest.

text.p: Thousands of impoverished Thai villagers were set to end a three-month-old protest in front of the country's Government House after making a deal with the government on Tuesday, officials and protesters said.

Villagers from the poor northeastern provinces prepared to dismantle their makeshift homes in front of Government House in Bangkok after the cabinet agreed to compensate them for land lost due to government development projects such as dams.
"We agreed to replace or compensate the people who can prove they have lost their land...mostly from the dams," government spokesman Amnaj Chanawong told a news conference after the cabinet meeting.
"The Assembly of the Poor said they were satisfied with the deal and agreed to return home," he added.

The Assembly of the Poor is the group of activists that organised the villagers, who had also demanded that the government free them from their long-standing debts to the state-owned Bank of Agriculture and Cooperatives and pay higher prices for their produce.
The spokesman said the government had agreed in principle to most of the demands made by the protesters.
About 15,000 villagers have lived in front of Government House since January and staged several street rallies to drum up support.

"We will have a final meeting with the government representative later today to work out how to implement the deal. If we have a guarantee from the government we will disperse and go home as soon as possible," Viraphol Sopha, a spokesman for the Assembly of the Poor, told reporters.
